subject: Host vs Incumbent: p95/p99 E2E Latency Qualification — Discovery Recap & Proposed Traffic Mix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Marsh <alex@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Host vs Incumbent: p95/p99 E2E Latency Qualification — Discovery Recap & Proposed Traffic Mix

Alex — thanks for a focused call today. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we all have the same picture.

Recap (what we heard)
- BluePeak target: p95 end-to-end <= 120 ms, p99 <= 450 ms for the short-path queries (user prompts up to ~64 tokens).
- Longer generation paths (200-600 tokens) acceptable up to p95 <= 350 ms and p99 <= 1.2s, but these are only ~12% of traffic.
- Streaming / partial-response UX is enabled for the longer paths; you expect clients to maintain up to 120 concurrent streaming sessions at peak.
- Baseline steady load ~180 requests/sec (RPS) with typical request size in the 8–40 token range; peak bursts up to ~850 RPS for 60s windows during business hours.
- Tail sensitivity: most user pain occurs when p99 spikes > 1s for short-path queries.

Questions we raised / outstanding items
1) Please confirm the traffic mix (short vs medium vs long) we discussed — we'll use a CSV sample for the hosted eval.
2) Are there hard SLAs required for p99 (credits/penalties) vs acceptance gate for PoC?
3) Any restrictions on regional routing (you said primary US-west, with EU read-only copies)?

Proposed next steps (high level)
- BluePeak: share the sample traffic profile CSV and a short list of representative prompts (preferably redacted).
- Redwood: run a 48-hour hosted probe that replays your traffic envelope (p95/p99 measurement for both short and long paths) and provide a transparent token-by-token latency breakdown.
- Schedule a 60-minute demo window next week where Redwood runs the live probe and we walk through the latency waterfall and fallback behavior.
- Agree on acceptance criteria for the demo: p95/p99 targets above for short-path (must meet p95 <=120ms and p99 <=450ms for >=95% of the 48-hour windows).

Attachments (attached to follow-up): bluepeak_traffic_profile.csv (sample envelope), slo_matrix_v1.pdf (proposed acceptance matrix).

I copied Ben & Logan for the technical handoff. Ben — can you confirm resource/instance sizing and whether we should suggest an initial canary slice (10% traffic) or a shadow probe?

Alex — if the above looks right, can you drop the sample CSV into the Drive link and propose two 60-minute windows next week (ideally Tue/Wed mornings PST)?

—Marissa
Customer Success / Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Host vs Incumbent: p95/p99 E2E Latency Qualification — Discovery Recap & Proposed Traffic Mix

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap and yes, that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Traffic mix: short (<=64 tokens) ~72%, medium (65–200 tokens) ~16%, long (>200 tokens) ~12%. I'll upload a 24-hour sample trace (anonymized) as the CSV.
- SLA: our procurement team prefers acceptance gates rather than formal financial credits for the PoC; we want objective pass/fail for go/no-go. If we move to a contract we will re-open SLA/credits discussion.
- Regions: primary region us-west; EU region only for batch analytics (no live inference).
- Streaming concurrency: 120 concurrent streaming sessions is the realistic worst-case.

Available demo windows (PST): Wed 2026-05-20 09:00–10:00 or Thu 2026-05-21 10:00–11:00. We prefer Wed if that works.

I'll upload the sample CSV to the Drive link you shared and add a short README with representative prompt categories. Expect that upload by EOD tomorrow (Wed).

—Alex
Director of Product
BluePeak Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Host vs Incumbent: p95/p99 E2E Latency Qualification — Discovery Recap & Proposed Traffic Mix

Looping in a few technical notes based on Marissa/Alex thread: 

1) Probe plan: for the hosted probe we'll replay at the per-second granularity from the CSV. We'll include both cold-start scenarios (no cache) and warmed KV-cache runs; that gives a realistic envelope for p99 behavior.
2) Suggested canary: start with a shadow probe for 24 hours, then a 10% live canary for 4 hours if the shadow pass looks good. Canary config: 2 x A100-equivalent workers in region us-west, batching config tuned for 16–64 token short requests, dynamic batching window 5–8ms.
3) Streaming: to validate 120 concurrent streaming sessions we should run a scaled streaming probe (simulate partial chunking and client ack behavior). That will expose buffering-induced tail latency.
4) Monitoring hooks: we'll attach token-level timestamps, request-trace ids, and a p95/p99 rolling window (5m/1h) to the demo dashboard. Need BluePeak to confirm any internal trace headers we should copy through.

If the acceptance gate is an objective pass/fail, we should define exact measurement windows and the allowed number of outlier events per 24-hour block. Proposal: for short-path: across the 48-hour probe, require that at least 90% of half-hour windows have p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 450ms. If that passes, move to 10% canary.

Logan — can you draft the demo runbook and expected instance sizing (I can provide a quick cost estimate for the PoC)?

—Ben
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
